Executive summary
This framework sets out practical guidance for organisations that deploy automated decision
systems in the public and private sectors. It explains how organisations can govern the use of
these systems, manage the risks they create, and communicate clearly with the people they
affect, in line with existing law.

The framework is voluntary. It does not replace any legal obligation.

1. Introduction
Automated decision systems are used to approve loans, screen applicants and set prices. This
section explains why governance matters and who the framework is for.

2. Scope of the framework
The framework applies to any organisation that uses an automated decision system to make or
support a decision about an individual. It covers the whole life of a system, from design to
retirement.

• Organisations should assign clear roles and responsibilities for each automated decision system.
• Organisations should assess the risk of harm to individuals before deployment.
• Organisations should keep records of the testing and monitoring of each system.
• Short bullet
• Organisations should give individuals a way to ask for human review of a decision.

3. Risk assessment and testing
Organisations should test each system before and after deployment.
